ceviri.20: Why is Shopify SEO work run differently from WordPress/WooCommerce?
ceviri.21: Because on Shopify, access to the server and the core code is closed, and optimization is done through Liquid templates and the app layer. The direct interventions made at plugin level on WooCommerce move here to the channels the platform permits, and that changes the planning of the work from the outset.
ceviri.22: Which takes more priority in SEO terms, the category page or the product page?
ceviri.23: As a general rule category pages come first, because of the internal link flow and the broad keywords they cover. That priority can change with the store's product range and the distribution of search volume, so a priority map by page type is drawn up at the start of the work.
ceviri.24: If the store platform is changed, does the SEO work start from scratch?
ceviri.25: When the platform changes, the URL structure and the technical constraints change with it, so some steps are rebuilt. But the foundations — keyword research and content strategy — can usually be carried over; a correct 301 redirect plan keeps the loss during the move to a minimum.
ceviri.26: Can product descriptions cause a duplicate content problem, and how is that prevented?
ceviri.27: Using the ready-made product descriptions supplied by a distributor word for word means the same text repeats across dozens of stores. That risk is reduced with original description templates and canonical redirects on variant pages.
ceviri.28: Is e-commerce SEO work affected by stock and price updates?
ceviri.29: Yes — frequent stock and price changes mean the page content and the structured data have to stay current. If products that are out of stock aren't given the right redirect or availability markup, search engines can assess the page on faulty signals.
ceviri.30: Which of Shopify's technical SEO constraints can't be got around?
ceviri.31: The basic URL structure and some server-level settings are fixed by the platform and closed to outside intervention. We don't try to get around those constraints; instead we aim for the highest return in the areas the platform does allow.

ceviri.63: Why Technical SEO Works Differently on Shopify, ikas and IdeaSoft
ceviri.64: On a WordPress-based WooCommerce store you have direct access to the server and the core code, whereas on closed systems like Shopify those layers are locked by the platform.
ceviri.65: The Liquid template structure fixes the URL patterns and the directory hierarchy in advance; the classic drop-a-file-in-the-root approach simply doesn't apply here. Canonical tag management, redirect rules and schema markup are mostly handled through the app ecosystem, so an intervention made without knowing which app injects which code can create a clash. On ikas and IdeaSoft the theme engine and the API constraints behave differently again — the same technical recipe doesn't give the same result on two platforms.
ceviri.67: Category Page or Product Page — Which Gets Optimized First?
ceviri.68: In terms of traffic potential, category pages are usually ahead, because they gather a broad set of keywords onto one page and sit at the centre of the internal link flow.
ceviri.69: Product pages, on the other hand, are closer to conversion and match more specific, long-tail searches. The order of priority also depends on how the faceted navigation is built; uncontrolled filter combinations can produce thousands of thin variation pages and scatter the crawl budget. Canonical redirects and the decision on selective indexing are the real factors that set the SEO value of the category architecture. ceviri.119: Faceted Navigation and Crawl Budget Management
ceviri.120: The endless page variations produced by filter combinations can weaken the crawl that search engines allocate to the store's important pages. In this work, which combination should be indexed and which should be merged with a canonical redirect is decided page by page.
ceviri.122: Every colour, size or pack variation can produce its own URL; left unchecked, dozens of copies of the same product enter the index. Canonical tagging and variant grouping logic gather that repetition onto a single strong page.
ceviri.123: The Redirect Plan for a Platform Move
ceviri.124: When the store platform changes, mapping the old URLs to the new structure keeps the page authority that has built up from being lost. The redirect plan is prepared in advance, broken down by product and category, and indexing is followed after the move.
